scope: Operation-specific uses of redundancy in Hodgson manuscript and zoological infrastructures.

records.operation: request multiple copies of same Buddhist texts
records.problem_being_verified: scribal error and ambiguous textual reading
records.mechanism: compare two or more partially independent copies to stabilize difficult passages
records.source_status: published transcription/citation of Burnouf letter; archive letter also catalogued
archive_tests: map requested copies to surviving shelfmarks

records.operation: multiple acknowledgements of same three-crate arrival
records.mechanism: independent or separate institutional acknowledgements corroborate arrival of shipment units
records.source_status: RAS archival descriptions of Burnouf 15 Jul and Mohl 29 Jul letters

records.operation: retain complete comparative series while separating obvious duplicates
records.mechanism: institution keeps representative skull/horn/bone series after comparison

records.operation: create numbered specimen series for other recipients
records.problem_being_verified: distributed access to representative zoological material
records.mechanism: museum comparison/selection converts received multiples into destination-specific series

records.operation: send catalogue copies to institutions that received duplicate specimens
records.problem_being_verified: shared interpretation/identification of separated specimen sets
records.mechanism: metadata copies are distributed along physical duplicate network
records.source_status: ZSL direct archival transcription of Hodgson to Forshall

general_rule: Never code duplicate/redundant objects without an operation-specific purpose where evidence permits.
cross_domain_claim: Controlled redundancy can make distributed knowledge more auditable, but its epistemic function differs by operation: textual collation, custody confirmation, reference comparison, physical distribution, or metadata synchronization.
failure_warning: Redundancy creates additional identity-management requirements; copies/specimens/catalogues can diverge, collide, or lose their relations even while multiplication increases available witnesses.
